clue.text: Kids grabbing parent's front or back

indicators.note: the kids hold on to the letter, so it goes inside them

parts.note: kids here are sons, a family's boys

indicators.note: a word's front is its first letter, here of parent's

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Children cling to a mum or dad, either in front or behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'front or back' reads as a pair of positions, but 'front' is only the first-letter signal and 'back' is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To back a person or event is to support it with money, the same as underwriting it.

clue.text: Aired jumper on box (notice rest splitting)

indicators.note: the rest breaks the notice word apart, sitting in its middle

parts.note: to spy something is to notice it
kip is British slang for sleep or a rest

explanation.surface: A broadcast jumper is worn on a box, with a note splitting the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' is not a sweater but a kangaroo: Skippy the Bush Kangaroo was an Australian TV series shown widely in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: The television kangaroo was a leaping animal broadcast on the small screen, a jumper on TV.

clue.text: Clothes not in the closet match

parts.note: someone open about being gay is out, no longer in the closet
to fit is to match or suit

explanation.surface: Clothes that are not kept in the wardrobe still go well together.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of garments worn together is an ensemble, a set of clothes.

clue.text: Small runners struggle in last metres

indicators.note: the letters of last metres struggle and writhe into another order

explanation.surface: Short-legged athletes battle on in the closing metres of a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runners' are not athletes but flowing water.
explanation.definitionFit: Water that runs is a stream, so little streams are small runners.

clue.text: Con man's side-splitting accents

indicators.note: the sides are split off, so the word loses its first and last letters

parts.note: brogues are broad regional accents, especially Irish

explanation.surface: A con man has a hilarious way with accents.
explanation.walkthrough: 'side-splitting' looks like 'very funny' but takes off the outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A swindling rascal is a dishonest scoundrel, much like a confidence trickster.

clue.text: In September, the dog's tied up

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the run of letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Every September someone keeps their dog on a lead.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across SeptemBER, THE and Dog's.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship that is moored at its dock has been tied up there, that is, given a berth.

clue.text: With short boat, beauty catches carp

indicators.note: the beauty catches the boat, holding it inside

parts.note: a belle is a beautiful woman

indicators.note: cut short, the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a yacht is a sailing boat

explanation.surface: A beauty in a small boat lands a carp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carp' is not a fish but a verb, to grumble.
explanation.definitionFit: To carp is to complain persistently, and to whinge about trifles is the slang meaning here.

clue.text: Noises from 19th group back?

parts.note: a row is a line of seats, a group going back from the front of a theatre
S is the 19th letter, so the 19th row from row A is labelled S

explanation.surface: A query about what sounds come from the nineteenth set of people further back.
explanation.walkthrough: Theatre rows are lettered A, B, C... from the front, so the 19th going back is row S. 'Noises' means quarrels or din, rhyming with cows.
explanation.definitionFit: A row is a loud quarrel or racket, so noisy disturbances are plural of that sense.

clue.text: Husband's theory: road leads to escape

parts.note: an idea is a theory
a way is a road

explanation.surface: A husband's theory about the road ahead leads to an escape route.
explanation.definitionFit: A secluded retreat is a place to get away to, an escape from everyday life.

clue.text: Drawback of wind does for resort

indicators.note: to re-sort is to sort the letters of wind does again

explanation.surface: The disadvantage of wind for a holiday resort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' looks like a holiday place but is read as re-sort.
explanation.definitionFit: A disadvantage or negative aspect of something is its drawback.

clue.text: Bury Football Club

definitions.meaning: to bury a body is to put it in a grave
... Milan is an Italian football club, often called just ...

explanation.surface: Bury Football Club is a real English team, from the town of Bury near Manchester.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter is to place in a grave, and Inter is the Milan football side, so both senses fit.

clue.text: She's abandoned for driving surprise sell in recession, papers assumed

indicators.note: receding means going back, so the word is written backwards

parts.note: to flog something is slang for selling it

indicators.note: the exclamation takes on the papers, holding them inside

parts.note: wow is a cry of surprise
ID, identity papers

explanation.surface: A shock sale in an economic downturn, with paperwork taken on board, all on a car journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'driving' is not motoring but hitting a golf ball from the tee.
explanation.definitionFit: A wife left alone while her husband plays golf all weekend is jokingly called this; she is deserted for the game.

clue.text: Investigator playing every tape first for impact

indicators.note: the letters of every tape, with one more added, are played around with into a new order
only the first letter of impact is used

explanation.surface: Someone runs every tape first to see how it hits home.
explanation.definitionFit: A detective hired privately rather than from the police is an investigator by trade.

clue.text: Dated briefly, making move

indicators.note: cut short, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: ...é means out of date

explanation.surface: Someone who dated for a short time ends up moving on.
explanation.definitionFit: In football or chess a pass is a move, sending the ball or turn on to another.

clue.text: Army, perhaps, taking time in bad weather? Definitely!

parts.note: an army is an example of a force

indicators.note: the time abbreviation sits inside the bad weather

parts.note: rain is bad weather

explanation.surface: Would an army spend time out in foul weather? Certainly.
explanation.definitionFit: Without any doubt, assuredly: said to stress that something is certain.

clue.text: Media editor not oddly involved in his work

definitions.text: Media editor not oddly involved in his work

parts.words: Media editor not oddly involved in his work
parts.note: drop the odd letters of media editor and E I E I O remains, the refrain of the nursery song about the farmer whose work is his farm

explanation.surface: A newspaper's media editor, rather oddly, is caught up in some job.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking away the 1st, 3rd, 5th... letters of 'Media editor' leaves EIEIO, which features in the song of the farmer who 'had a farm'; the clue points to him by that refrain.
explanation.definitionFit: The farmer of the children's song is famous for the chorus E-I-E-I-O sung about his farm.

clue.text: Set dimmer switches labelled incorrectly

indicators.note: switching means swapping round, so the letters of set dimmer change places

explanation.surface: Light switches marked dimmer were given the wrong labels.
explanation.definitionFit: To give something the wrong name is to misname or misterm it, labelling it wrongly.

clue.text: Wet starts to summers quite upsetting — everyone loves comparatively hot years

indicators.note: the start of each following word is taken

explanation.surface: A wet summer is upsetting, yet everyone loves the hot years.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground that is sodden and squishes underfoot is wet and soggy.

clue.text: Want 3 down by hotel that's seen in forest

parts.note: to pine for something is to want it

indicators.note: the number is down by the letter, that is, short of it

parts.note: the number written as a word
H is hotel in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Wanting the third down clue's answer by the hotel, in a forest.
explanation.walkthrough: '3 down' looks like a reference to another clue, but it is just the number three, with 'down by hotel' losing its H.
explanation.definitionFit: A conifer bearing needles and cones is common in woodland, so it is something seen in a forest.

clue.text: Perfect example of sequence isn't complex

indicators.note: something complex is intricate and tangled, so the letters of sequence isn't are tangled up

explanation.surface: A sequence that is not complicated is held up as a model.
explanation.definitionFit: The purest, most typical instance of something is its essence distilled, a model case.

clue.text: British couple carrying on about superhuman

indicators.note: the couple carries on within it

parts.note: two in Roman numerals is II
taken as written
C, short for circa, about

explanation.surface: A British pair go on about something beyond human.
explanation.definitionFit: With electronic body parts giving extraordinary powers, a cyborg hero is superhuman.

clue.text: Grease monkeys in suits

indicators.note: to monkey with is to tamper, so the letters of grease are tampered with

explanation.surface: Mechanics, grease monkeys, wearing business suits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suits' looks like clothing but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: If an arrangement suits you it is acceptable, it fits or goes along with you.

clue.text: More than one viewer is heard

indicators.note: said out loud, the plural of the letter I is the same as the body parts that see

parts.note: read as I's, the plural of the letter I

explanation.surface: A sentence fragment saying that many people watching can be heard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is' is read as I's, more than one letter I, and spoken it sounds the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An eye is the organ that views, so a pair of them is more than one viewer.

clue.text: Associating bum-wiggling ban with one extremely moved

indicators.note: the outer letters of one, O and E, are moved, swapping places

parts.note: twerking is wiggling one's bottom while dancing; a ban on it is no twerking

explanation.surface: A prohibition on twerking is passed, with someone very emotional about it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one extremely' gives O and E, the ends of 'one'; 'moved' swaps where they sit in NO TWERKING.
explanation.definitionFit: Mixing with others to make useful business contacts is mingling or associating for profit.

clue.text: Name of chap going up the A1?

parts.note: the A1 is a major British road, one way to the north
going up the country leads to the North-East, NE, of Britain

explanation.surface: What do you call a man who drives north on the A1?
explanation.walkthrough: The A1 is Britain's longest numbered road, running from London up to Edinburgh through the North-East of England.
explanation.definitionFit: A male first name, as borne by John Wayne, so it is the name of a man.

clue.text: 50 like peas in clump

indicators.note: the number is put inside the pod

parts.note: peas are found in a pod
L is 50 in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Fifty or so peas packed into a cluster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'like peas in' recalls 'like peas in a pod'; 'clump' is a verb, to walk heavily.
explanation.definitionFit: To trudge along heavily and slowly is to stomp or clump.

clue.text: My whitewash is embraced by Labour leader losing election in the end

indicators.note: the whitewash goes inside the shortened leader's name
the last letter of election is dropped from the name

parts.note: Jeremy Corbyn led the UK Labour Party when the puzzle appeared

indicators.note: the end of election is its last letter

parts.note: limewash is whitewash, so lime is a whitewash

explanation.surface: A whitewashing of the Labour leader as he loses an election at last.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My' is not a pronoun but the exclamation of surprise. The answer is a British exclamation of astonishment.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are cries of surprise; the British slang exclamation is a twisted form of God blind me.

clue.text: Filmed orphan taking relatives inside

indicators.note: taking off the outer letters of the word
only the inside of the word is kept

parts.note: nannies, a child's word for grandmothers

explanation.surface: An orphan in a film is adopted by relatives who take her in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking ... inside' means keep only the inner letters of NANNIES, losing N and S. The musical about the little orphan girl was filmed in 1982.
explanation.definitionFit: Little Orphan Annie, heroine of a comic strip and musical, was brought to the screen.

clue.text: Gave up (did bear?)

definitions.meaning: produced, as a tree does fruit or a field bears a crop

explanation.definitionFit: To surrender is to give in, and a crop that produced fruit gave a harvest; both are senses of the word.

clue.text: They can't bear young European students grouped round church

parts.note: EU, the European Union

indicators.note: the students go round the church, holding it inside

parts.note: NUS, the National Union of Students, students joined together

explanation.surface: Young European students in a group around a church can't stand young people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bear' looks like 'tolerate'; it means give birth to.
explanation.definitionFit: Castrated men cannot father children, so they are unable to produce offspring.
